::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Traces to the state-owned Nantong Transistor Factory; its largest shareholder is the state-linked Nantong Huada Microelectronics Group (18.80% as of June 2026). The Big Fund, which once held as much as 21.72%, has been selling down since 2020 and held 5.00% by June 2026. In 2016, Tongfu and the Big Fund jointly paid $371 million for 85% stakes in AMD's Suzhou and Penang assembly and test facilities — a rare case of a Chinese OSAT firm acquiring a Western chipmaker's own packaging plants outright. H1 2026 revenue reached ¥16 billion (+23% YoY) with net profit up 317% YoY to ¥1.72 billion; Q2 2026 net profit alone was ¥1.39 billion, up 346.9% year-on-year.
:::

**Chinese name:** 通富微电 (Tōngfù Wēidiàn)

## What does this facility make?

At Nantong: flip-chip (FC) and system-in-package (SiP) packaging for high-performance computing and communications chips at the Sutong plant, and 8/12-inch wafer-level packaging (copper pillar, solder bump, WLCSP) at the Chongchuan headquarters. Tongfu's most advanced work, 7nm/5nm FCBGA and chiplet integration for AMD, is done at its Suzhou and Penang subsidiaries (TF-AMD), not in Nantong, according to the company's 2026 prospectus.

## Why does it matter?

One of two mainland Chinese firms in the world's top five OSAT companies by revenue (JCET is the other) — reporting describes Tongfu as one of three Chinese firms that have begun HBM packaging, a capability central to AI-accelerator supply chains. Tongfu also handles over 80% of AMD's global CPU/GPU packaging and test orders, with AMD alone accounting for about 52.3% of Tongfu's total revenue. That dependence cuts both ways: it is the clearest evidence of a Chinese OSAT firm embedded deep in the global AI-memory supply chain, and a concentration risk if AMD diversifies.

## Packaging Technology Trajectory

- **2025**: Nantong Sutong plant: FC/SiP HPC packaging line (2022 issue) built out
- **2026**: Nantong Chongchuan HQ: 8/12in wafer-level (Cu pillar, bump, WLCSP), as of

## Project Timeline

- **Jan 2016** — Tongfu and the Big Fund jointly acquire 85% equity stakes in AMD's Suzhou and Penang assembly and test facilities for $371 million
- **Jul 2026** — Reports H1 2026 revenue of ¥16 billion (+23% YoY) and net profit of ¥1.72 billion (+317% YoY), crediting HBM and AMD-related advanced packaging volume
